scenes.intro: Hello Samantha. Your financial health score is 82 out of 100, a strong result. Over the next few scenes you will see your plan as a home, with each part showing what is solid, cracked or broken.
scenes.pillar_savings_and_cash_flow: Your plumbing is solid. Savings and cash flow score 22 out of 30 points. You save $60,000 a year, 24% of income, but the yearly flow is $6,418 short, so the habit is strong while the money is not aimed at retirement or college. Your $80,000 cash covers 7.9 months of essentials, though little slack is left after near-term goals.
scenes.pillar_debt: Your walls are solid. Debt scores 20 out of 20 points. You have no debt, with a balance of $0, and your home is owned outright with $900,000 in equity. That keeps your income free for college and retirement, though your cushion is thin after near-term goals.
scenes.pillar_investments: Your garden is cracked. Investments score 10 out of 15 points. Your invested savings are $335,000, with 85.1% in stocks against a target of 80.0%, so the garden grows but leans a little more on the weather than you planned. With $0 in 529 plans and no retirement accounts, college and retirement both pull on the same cash.
scenes.pillar_liquidity_and_emergency_fund: Your foundations are solid. Your emergency fund scores 15 out of 15 points. Your $80,000 cash covers 7.9 months of essential expenses, above the 5 to 6 months recommended. Once you set aside $18,500 for near-term goals, cover drops to 6.1 months, so the cushion is real but thinner than it first looks.
scenes.pillar_insurance_and_protection: Your roof is solid. Insurance and protection score 14 out of 20 points. You hold $2,000,000 of term life insurance and a $2,000,000 umbrella policy that stands behind your home and auto cover. Still, that home and auto cover shows as uninsured, so it is worth confirming.
scenes.move_1: Your plan already worked out adding homeowners insurance on your primary home to close a gap in your cover. That repair is for your roof, and it moves your score from 82 out of 100 to 84 out of 100.
scenes.move_2: Your plan already worked out spreading out the money you hold in one single fund, moving VTI from 39% to 25% of your market holdings, about $58,300 of that fund. That repair is for your garden, and it lifts your score from 82 out of 100 to 83 out of 100.
scenes.move_3: Your plan already worked out shifting the mix of your investments from 85% growth to 80% growth, about $17,100 of what you have invested. That repair is for your garden, and it moves your score from 82 out of 100 to 83 out of 100.
scenes.timeline: Looking ahead, you plan to retire at 65, and on the current plan your savings and investments run out at age 73. The plan also has no debt from 2059 onward.
